title: Article 1: REGACE and agrivoltaics
summary: Present Antonucci et al. (2025): how farmers in five countries were involved in shaping agrivoltaic greenhouses.
checklist: Read the article, at least the abstract, methods, Table 1 and the discussion
Go through the slides and their speaker notes
Rehearse once with a timer: 10 minutes
Pick one discussion question to ask the class

title: Steps 1 and 2: the problem and the stakeholders
summary: Define the innovation problem and map its stakeholder ecosystem. Deliverables A (Context Brief) and B (Ecosystem Map).
asks: Step 1: What is the technology and what problem should it solve? Who develops or promotes it? Where will it be implemented? What benefits are expected? What uncertainties, risks or controversies may emerge? Why is participation necessary?
Step 2: Map actors, interests, knowledge, power, vulnerability and missing voices.

Required visual: the innovation at the centre; stakeholders by proximity, influence and impact; connections for alliances, dependencies, conflicts and knowledge flows; vulnerable actors highlighted; a short reason why each actor should participate.
checklist: Be able to explain the idea in two sentences: AI assistant + fairness rule written by tenants
Know why the third function (sharing the money) is what makes it new
Learn the map: who is close, who holds power, who is vulnerable, who is missing
Read the Context Brief (A) once

title: Article 2: social and digital vulnerabilities
summary: Present Antonucci, Sorice and Volterrani (2022): participation in Italy's peripheral, "liminal" areas and the role of digital capital.

materials.title: Original article (PDF)
materials.note: Frontiers in Political Science 4 (2022) · CC BY 4.0

checklist: Read the article, at least the introduction, Tables 1 to 3 and the conclusions
Understand the two key concepts: liminal space and digital capital
Rehearse once with a timer: 10 minutes
Note that Tor Bella Monaca appears in the paper: it links straight to our project

title: Article 3 and Steps 3 to 4
summary: Present van Oudheusden et al. (2024) on citizen sciences, then co-define the participatory challenge and decide the levels of participation.

materials.note: From the developers' problem to a shared question
Five levels, seven phases, four binding gates

asks: Step 3: Write the original problem formulation. Imagine what different actors might add or contest. Rewrite the problem as a shared participatory question.
Step 4: Different phases may need different levels: inform, consult, involve, co-design, co-create.
checklist: Read Article 3 (it is a short discussion paper)
Learn our shared participatory question by heart
Know the four gates and when they happen (months 2, 4, 4 and 7)
Be ready for: "Why not co-create everything?"

title: Steps 5 and 6: methods and hybrid design
summary: Choose methods by purpose and design the hybrid architecture. Deliverables C (Participation Blueprint) and E (Hybrid Journey Map).
asks: Step 5: Choose methods because they perform a task: explore, open the agenda, deliberate, generate ideas, produce knowledge, test and adapt.

Step 6: For every phase, on-site, online or both? Synchronous and asynchronous moments. How information moves between settings. Digital tools for continuity, not to copy meetings. Alternatives for low digital skills.
Journey Map: before, on-site, online and after, with the connections between moments.
checklist: For each method, say the task it performs in one sentence
Explain the 48-hour rule and the energy ambassadors
Walk through the Journey Map out loud
Read the Participation Blueprint (C): it is 30% of the grade

title: Book 4: co-creation
summary: Present Phillips (2025), Embracing the Messy Complexities of Co-Creation.

materials.title: Book 4 slides
materials.note: We need the book PDF to prepare these

checklist: Share the book PDF with the group
Read the assigned chapters

title: Step 7: citizen science
summary: "Energy Detectives": tenants produce the knowledge the AI is missing. Deliverable D.
asks: Formulate research questions. Say what citizens will observe, measure, document, classify or interpret. Who defines the protocol and how is data quality addressed? Include collective interpretation. Show how citizen knowledge influences design, implementation or governance.
Avoid the extractive model: no unpaid sensors; clear data ownership and privacy; recognise local knowledge; return results; a way to challenge findings.
checklist: Know RQ1 to RQ3 and the decision each one feeds
Explain the wide and deep tracks
Walk through the five steps from a postcard to a change in the AI
Read the Citizen Science document (D)

title: Step 8: the prototype
summary: The Fair Share Simulator: tenants try fairness rules on real-looking families before they vote. Deliverable F.

materials.note: What it is, the rules, how we test it

asks: Make one part of the process tangible. The prototype should be usable or testable, not merely described. Explain what you would learn by testing it with real participants.
checklist: Try the simulator yourself before class
Know the four rules: Equal, Need, Effort, Floor
Be ready to demo one scenario live

title: Step 9: facilitation and inclusion
summary: Reaching beyond the usual participants, and keeping the room fair.
asks: Recruitment, accessibility, power balance, conflict, traceability and feedback.
checklist: Know how we reach each hard-to-reach group
Explain "experts on tap, not on top"
Answer: what happens if tenants disagree with the developers?

title: Final exam: Step 10 and the pitch
summary: Written exam (two questions) and the 10-minute project pitch. Deliverables G (Evaluation) and H (Final Pitch).
asks: Do not evaluate only satisfaction or numbers. Measure the quality and diversity of participation, whether different kinds of knowledge entered, learning and trust, and above all what changed in the technology because of participation.
Pitch: 1 min technology, 2 min stakeholders, 2 min hybrid architecture, 2 min citizen science and prototype, 1 min what changes, 1 min evaluation, 1 min risk.
checklist: Rehearse the pitch with a timer, twice
Practise the professor's seven questions (see the Project page)
Revise the three articles and Book 4 for the written questions
Read the Evaluation document (G)
